text:
Karen: Velari POC on Dedicated pool (us-west) reporting very slow TTFT today — go-to-prod demo blocked tomorrow morning. 1st request sometimes 3–4s. Logs show a bunch of kvcache misses and 429s. Anyone oncall?

Dan: I'm on. Can you paste the request id and sample logs?

Karen: request id: 0a9f3c. Minimal logs: 
```
[2026-03-20T16:12:01Z] req=0a9f3c model=redwood-xl size=2048 queue=slot1 kvcache=miss prefetch=false batch_id=178 rlimit=200
[2026-03-20T16:12:02Z] req=0a9f3c token=1 first_token_latency=3200ms total=3.2s status=200
[2026-03-20T16:12:02Z] pool=dedicated-usw congestion=high inflight=48 max_batch=8 throttle=429
```

Tony: We saw that pool spike last night; batching window got long because of affinity mismatch. Nora, could runtime confirm if prefill/kvcache policy for this customer got disabled?

Nora: Looking... I see Velari was on prefill policy 'aggressive-prefill-v2' but a config roll last week toggled 'prefill.enabled=false' for pooled customers with strict quotas — likely reverted. Rolling back this flag should help.

Maya: Sales asked about pricing if we need to bump reserved capacity — they want cost estimate for one extra p3 equivalence for the week.

Dan: Quick mitigation steps: set prefill.enabled=true, reduce max_batch_size to 4 for this pool, and set burst_concurrency=30. Also enable prefix cache warmup in routing.

Karen: How do we flip prefill back quickly? Any CLI?

Nora: Use internal tool:
```
# enable prefill for customer
redwoodctl customers update velari --set prefill.enabled=true --pool=dedicated-usw
# adjust pool batching
redwoodctl pools update dedicated-usw --set max_batch_size=4 --set burst_concurrency=30
```

Tony: I've applied a temporary patch to routing that prefers warm-q affinity. Give it 2–3 minutes.

Dan: Also note there were 429s tied to quota pressure — Velari has default per-customer qps limit 120. Increasing customer rate_limit to 400 temporarily helps:
```
redwoodctl customers update velari --set rate_limit.qps=400
```

Maya: Pricing note: extra reserved capacity would be $12k/month (approx) for single p3 equiv; temporary boost for demo -> $500/day. I'll loop finance.

Karen: After patches, first request is back to ~600ms. :tada: Can we follow up with a postmortem and checklist so this doesn't recur?

Tony: I'll open an incident and root-cause ticket. Initial hypothesis: config rollout toggled prefill flag + quota bump needed. We should add a preflight check for dedicated pool prefill=true for POCs.

Dan: I'll coordinate with Velari to reproduce the exact prompt set and get perf numbers. Thanks all.
